title: Freelancing in New York; Rutgers and the Childs job
summary: Dance notes recent years of freelancing. Thomas says he decided in the 1940s to develop his own playing, and that a man at a Rutgers dance got him the Childs Restaurant job.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, now in these last years, it's mostly been sort of since the time we were talking of, it's mostly been free lancing around New York.
Yeah, it's been rough but I mean that's really, I mean various things have come up and ...

... what has happened with me, I made a little decision back in the '40s so if I got a terrific one guy's note, with all due respect, see if I can play two more, three more and ... supposed to get together, let's see what happens. And, pardon me, I think I'm very happy about it because if you're prepared to give yourself expression and I have faith in one of the fellows that helped me along the way was a fellow from MCA and I could never forget him, (Junior Wist (?)). I was over here at Rutgers and ... had some bands over there, some pretty good bands. And, it rained like hell that night. So a fellow came in from somewhere so they had a big ballroom out there (and the cats could come ...) dancing. So a fellow comes in, he's got a uniform on. He said, I know you. And

I said, You do? Where from? I'd gone over and had this thing over here ... where/you go to get that punch and all that kind of business so I'm going to have some punch, you know. ... make a long story short, he was from a band in New York and we got to talking and he gave me just as much inspiration; he said I know you drew worked for a long time and get in there and we do some people out there, you know, a big audience, around 5,000 people we had in there who drove out to listen to what we were doing. ... that's how I got Childs Restaurant.
